content.name: p
children: Webhooks invert the usual development loop. Instead of your code calling an API, a provider calls your code — which means it needs a public HTTPS URL, real events, and a valid signature before your handler runs at all. Good providers recognize this and give developers ways to close that feedback loop.

frontmatter.title: Testing and Local Development
frontmatter.description: Webhooks are hard to test because the provider has to reach your code. Tunnels, provider CLIs, test events, and delivery logs close the feedback loop for webhook consumers.
